articleTitle: Empowering Resilient Hospital Microgrids in Gaza with a Novel Toolbox for Sustainable Energy Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative improvement in a in fieri decision support strategy (DSS) aimed at supporting the selection of indicators designed for the energy management strategy for sizing resilient isolated microgrids (RIM) navigating energy challenges within conflict zones. A unique feature of this proposed approach involves a combination of established guidelines for sizing batteries, photovoltaic (PV) systems, and wind turbines, in tandem with the integration of a predictive tool and a consolidated, optimized energy management system. The decisive decision-making process of identifying optimal Days of Autonomy, indicative of the system's capacity to autonomously meet load demands through a careful balance of various technical considerations, constitutes a cornerstone of this investigation. The paper carefully examines the methodology, outcomes, and following discussions, with a particular focus on the deployment of innovative key performance indicators and their synergistic amalgamation. The Kamal Adwan Hospital in Gaza serves as the focal point of the case study, supplemented by a laboratory test bench for validation.

articleTitle: Concept and Preliminary Design of a Stand-Alone Charging Station for Light Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive overview for the design, development, and implementation of a standalone charging station tailored for light electric vehicles. The project unfolds in several distinct phases, each essential for the success-ful realization of the standalone charging station. The initial phase presented in this work consists in the definition of the main characteristics of the station in terms of purpose, mode of use, expected impacts, electrical power supply, smart capabilities, and minimum quality of services to offer. After a brief presentation of the preliminary technological structure of the station, impact analysis is presented for a hypothetical dissemination of the station in various strategic points, such as weakly electrified areas or locations with occasional but high-density vehicle presence. The study concludes with a description of the subsequent project phases and the milestones planned for each of them, such as gathering feedback from stakeholders, optimal sizing of renewable power supply, components identifi-cation, prototyping, laboratory and field testing.

articleTitle: Field Test and Operation of Utility-Scale Battery Energy Storage System for Fast Frequency Response
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Fast frequency response (FFR) of the Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) is an effective way to mitigate the grid frequency deviations induced by the fluctuation of power generation from the variable renewable energy resources and the reduced system inertia caused by decreased number of synchronous generators. According to the above trends, several grid operators have launched the scheme of the procurement of FFR resources from the market, by specifying the technical requirements of FFR such as response speed, the deadband, and droop coefficient. Although there are many researchers investigating the effect of the FFR characteristics on the grid frequency stabilization, most of them have been performed based on either of offline time domain simulation or hardware-in-the-loop simulation. This paper exhibits the operational waveform of the 49.5MW utility-scale BESS in GB, which started the commercial operation in July-2023 in GB. In addition, the field experimental results of FFR with various FFR characteristics are shown in order to study the effect of the response speed and the droop characteristics of FFR on the BESS performance.

articleTitle: Control System Design for Grid-Forming Inverters in Grids with Background Harmonic Voltages
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Grid-forming inverters play a crucial role in reinforcing weak utility grids by assisting in maintaining standard voltage and frequency levels. However, their effectiveness can be compromised in grids with prevalent harmonic voltages, leading to potential degradation of the injected current. This paper introduces a novel method to address this challenge by refining the conventional dual-loop control system employed in grid-forming inverters. The proposed approach showcases the inverter's capability to effectively inject power into a grid even in the presence of significant background harmonics. Through simulations, the study substantiates the effectiveness of this method, presenting compelling results that underscore its superiority over conventional approaches. This innovative solution holds promise for enhancing the resilience and performance of grid-forming inverters in grids with heightened harmonic challenges.

articleTitle: Possible Schemes for the “Hypergrid” HVDC Switching Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The recent development of HVDC circuit breakers prototypes will enable meshed operation of dc grids, potentially introducing significant advantages and enhancing network operation if compared to typical, point-to-point dc links. Terna, the Italian Transmisison System Operator, has thus recently planned a new 500 kV HVDC network, to achieve the decar-bonization goals of the European Union's Fit for 55 initiative and Italy's National Energy and Climate Plan (PNIEC). This new “Hypergrid” project involve the construction of HVDC switching stations, equipped with dc breakers and hosting up to 10 bays. The paper exhamines possible station schemes for these switching stations, taking into account the novel needs for HVDC CBs maintenance and footprint constraints. Amongst the possible scheme, based on the single bus bar with transfer bus scheme, seems the most suitable compromise between the maintenability and availabily needs and the cost and footprint costraint. The use of a single transfer busbar, shared from both positive and negative poles leads to a “1 and 1/2 busbar scheme-single breaker”.

articleTitle: Smartphone-assisted Prepaid Meter System Using BLE IoT Sensors for Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Prepaid meter system provides consumers with better management of energy consumption. It also helps suppliers recover revenue by reducing operational cost and electricity fraud. However, a typical prepaid meter system has several limitations such as human intervention in credit recharging procedure and consumer's difficulty in figuring out the remaining credit balance; and utility company's difficulty in energy monitoring for customized services. This paper proposes a smartphone-assisted prepaid meter system using Bluetooth low energy (BLE) Internet of Things (IoT) sensors to over-come those limitations. A smartphone detects a prepaid meter based on proximity service, transfers purchased credits into the prepaid meter without human intervention. In addition, whenever consumers return home, using IoT sensors, their smartphone detects the prepaid meter, collects energy usage information and the remaining credit balance, and transfers them to the central server for energy monitoring. For feasibility analysis, latency for meter detection and probability of packet collision between neighboring meters are evaluated. The results show that a smartphone detects a prepaid meter, recharges it, and collects energy information in tens of seconds. Therefore, the smartphone-assisted prepaid meter system using BLE IoT sensors is shown to be feasible in real residential homes and expected to proliferate a prepaid meter system thanks to easy credit recharging and energy monitoring services without human intervention.

articleTitle: Series-Series Versus Series-Parallel in Terms of Stability Issues for Inductive Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The stable character of a system is given by its ability to provide a bounded response to the application of a bounded input signal. From the stability analysis point of view, several methods are proposed in the specialized literature. Many of these are based on the use of transfer functions, for which the poles values are then studied. In the present work, we started from one of these methods, which uses an admittance transfer function, to study stability issues of wireless power transfer systems. Two topologies are analyzed, namely series-series and series-parallel. The obtained results are presented in a comparative manner, emphasizing the advantages and disadvantages of each case.

articleTitle: Effect of Torque Load and Voltage Drop Observers on Robustness in Flatness-Based Control of PMSM Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Due to the nonlinear nature of the permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) drive system, its performance depends on the operational points when controlled using Proportional-Integral (PI)-based Field-oriented control (FOC). To deal with this issue, nonlinear control methods like ftatness-based control (FBC) have been proposed. This method usually utilizes voltage drop (in d- and q-axis) and load torque observers to improve its dynamic performance. In this paper, a robustness analysis based on the Jacobian matrix of the closed-loop model of the system has been performed to investigate the effect of these observers on the robustness of the FBC against variations in motor parameters. Both theoretical analysis and simulation studies show that the observers not only improve the dynamic performance of the control method, but also enhance the robust-ness of it significantly.

articleTitle: Method for Defining Electromagnetic Interferencies in the Metro Track Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The paper presents the analysis of electromagnetic environment on the Urban Rail Transport (Metro). The tonal track circuits with the automatic locomotive signaling and automatic speed regulation system are used to control traffic. The investigations of signaling currents and harmonics within the tonal track circuits (rail lines) were carried out. The method for evaluating of electromagnetic compatibility of tonal track circuits at the dc traction power system of 825 V with the track circuits was elaborated. This method involves measurements of signals at both the input and output of track circuits at the control points at the Post of Electric Centralizations.

Author Keywords: automatic locomotive signaling system with the automatic regulating speed (ALS-ARS system)

articleTitle: Influence of Interferences in the Relation Between Ampacity and Induced Voltage on Sheath in Double-Circuit Underground Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This paper discusses the relationship between ampacity and induced voltages within the context of the four widely adopted configurations in double-circuit underground lines. This analysis considers two scenarios: one that accounts for underground interferences, which is the most exact, and another that solely considers the separation typically used in these duct banks. The results show that, with greater cable installation depth, a larger separation between cables is required to guarantee ampacity. The dependence between these values depends on the physical arrangement of the duct banks. Nevertheless, if this separation increases, the induced voltage on the sheath also will increase. Furthermore, it is sufficient to utilize the usual separation and increase this result by at least 2% when calculating the induced voltage on the sheath rather than considering the augmentation in phase spacing caused by underground interferences.

articleTitle: Energy Consumption of Electric Buses Under Operational Data of Transit System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Urban adoption of electric buses prompts a need for optimized energy management. This study addresses the over-looked influence of operational data on battery electric buses (BEBs) energy consumption. It investigates which operational parameters significantly impact BEBs' energy usage and determines the most predictive data features. Employing Random Forest (RF) and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), the study develops regression models evaluated by RMSE, MSE, MAE, and R-squared metrics. Results indicate robust predictive performance with RF and XGBoost achieving RMSEs of 1.88 and 1.75, respectively. Euclidean distance between trip origins and destinations is identified as the key factor influencing energy consumption. The research enhances route planning and operational efficiency for BEBs, offering significant implications for reducing energy costs and supporting data-driven decisions in transit management.

articleTitle: Preliminary Results on the Impulse Breakdown Characteristics of Natural Ester Oil and Oil-Based Nanofluid with Fe2O3 Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This study presents an experimental investigation of the impulse breakdown characteristics of natural ester oil, in its pure form, and as the base liquid for a nanofluid with Fe203 nanoparticles (0.050% w/w). A two-stage impulse voltage generator and a combination wave generator have been used to determine the distribution of the breakdown voltage and time to breakdown; a standard test-cell per IEC 60897 and a custom-made metal fixture were employed for that purpose. Experimental results are discussed with emphasis given to the response time of the iron oxide nanofluid when compared to the base liquid.

articleTitle: Evaluating Voltage Unbalance Impact on Grid-Following Inverter Harmonic Emissions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: With the integration of renewables and increases in load demand, the power grid is constantly changing. This calls for some power quality standards to potentially be updated for the modern grid. Disturbances like harmonics and unbalance have an effect on one another, but that effect is not always considered in these standards. This work evaluates the impact of voltage unbalance on the harmonics produced by a grid- following inverter by performing a series of 15 simulations. These simulations consist of one grid voltage that is balanced, seven that are 2% unbalanced, and 7 that are 4% unbalanced. The resulting inverter voltage harmonics up to the 370<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> and the total harmonic distortion were recorded. Evaluation of these results showed that in the presence of voltage unbalance there were near-linear increases in the total harmonic distortion, notable increases in the characteristic and some non- characteristic harmonics, and minor increases in the low-order harmonics. This work opens the door for more extensive testing with the objective of developing equations relating harmonics to unbalance for the use of standardization.

articleTitle: Ground Fault Location Method for DC/DC Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Nowadays, using power electronics converters is essential for the correct operation of the electrical system. The use of this kind of devices, as inverters or rectifiers, makes the ground fault detection more complicated, specifically in the energy dissipation devices. This article presents a new method for ground fault detection and location in DC systems with DC/DC converters. It consists in analyzing the voltage signal of a grounding resistor that connects the neutral point of the system, which can be the AC neutral point of the star of the main power transformer or an artificial DC midpoint, and the ground. Analyzing the waveform of this voltage, the ground fault can be detected, and it can be determined which pole (positive or negative) is under fault condition. The new method has been validated through various simulations achieving desired results in each fault case.

articleTitle: On-Field Application of a Travelling Wave Based Fault Location Method for Unearthed Overhead Line Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: In this paper the on-field application of a single-ended fault location method for no-branched lines in unearthed operated networks is expounded. The method is based on the travelling wave theory, and it exploits the Continuous Wavelet Transformation to determine the dominant frequency of the earth mode component of the fault current. The paper represents the experimental validation of a novel fault location approach previously presented by the authors to the scientific community. In order to verify the accuracy of the method, phase-to-ground short circuits have been triggered on a real overhead line in different positions, since the on-field application of travelling wave-based fault location methods represents the more reliable bench test. In fact, the presence of inhomogeneities in the real transmission line structures significantly influences the travelling wave behaviour and they are quite difficult to represent in a simulation environment. The proposed algorithm proved to be reliable in the estimation of the fault distance.

articleTitle: Comparing Battery and Hybrid Diesel-Battery Freight Trains for Heavy Industrial
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The paper reports a feasibility study for a new railway line served by freight trains into an Industrial Complex located in Middle East region. The analysis compares hybrid and battery train solutions taken into account train performance simulations, with the scope to evaluate overall energy consumption of the system, considering the timetable for recharging locomotive, the key factor, benchmark and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> savings. The objective is to comprehensively characterize and analyze battery-powered and hybrid locomotives, conducting primary evaluations to assess their performance and suitability. Plano-altimetric characteristics of the line and the electro-mechanical characteristics of rolling stock are used as input data providing dynamic and kinematic profiles of the individual train as output. Thanks to this output it has been possible to estimate energy requirements, power of charging stations, state of charge, number of recharges, etc., for all freight trains in operation.

articleTitle: Is Selling the Oxygen Produced During Electrolysis Really a Solution to Make Green Hydrogen Cheaper?
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Institutions, companies, research centers and universities are paying special attention to green hydrogen, a key energy carrier for the decarbonization of various sectors because it is produced from renewable sources without producing emissions. Currently, however, the cost of producing it is high and does not make it competitive with that produced from fossil fuels. One way to cut costs could be to exploit the oxygen obtained as a by-product of water electrolysis, selling it instead of releasing it into the atmosphere as is usually done. In some studies, this idea has already been analyzed, but very often without considering the costs due to the additional components for treating the oxygen, which must be properly compressed and stored, or without directly showing how the LCOH (levelized cost of hydrogen) varies according to this choice, especially in an Italian context, limiting the study to an evaluation of the NPV. The paper analyzes plant configurations for the production of green hydrogen installed in southern Italy, in Sicily, in which a photovoltaic system powers an alkaline electrolyzer and two compressors: one for hydrogen and one for oxygen. The system is completed by the storage systems for the two gases. Levelized cost values for green hydrogen are calculated by considering the sale of oxygen either at prices found in the literature in similar studies, or at prices in the European Union for oxygen produced by air distillation, taking into account the operating and investment costs for the compressor and oxygen storage, and comparing the values obtained with the costs of green hydrogen without oxygen valorization.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation of PV-integrated Reconfigurable Microgrids and Computational Burden
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This paper addresses the significant potential of reconfiguration in renewable-based microgrids (MGs), emphasizing not only its practical benefits but also the computational challenges involved. Firstly, a nonlinear non-convex model developed for the optimal operation of photovoltaic (PV)-integrated reconfigurable microgrids (RMGs). To guarantee the optimality of the solutions, we further refine the model by extracting a mixed-integer linear programming model, achieved through the implementation of piecewise linearization technique and approximation. To substantiate the efficacy and importance of reconfiguration in MGs, comparative analyses of two distinct case studies-one with reconfiguration and one without are presented. These comparisons not only highlight the operational improvements afforded by reconfiguration but also shed light on the computational complexities encountered. Moreover, the impact of different radiality method selections on the computational time is explored. Our findings validate the significant role of reconfiguration in enhancing the performance of renewable-based MGs while also emphasizing the critical consideration of computational burden in the design and implementation of such systems.

articleTitle: Design Considerations and Energy Management System for Green and Reliable Telecommunication Base Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This paper presents the design considerations and optimization of an energy management system (EMS) tailored for telecommunication base stations (BS) powered by photovoltaic (PV) systems and battery energy storage systems (BESS). For the design considerations, the standards for critical loads are presented together with the required power quality. Later, we propose an EMS that minimizes the dependence on the grid and, therefore, the emissions. For the EMS a Model predictive control (MPC) algorithm is employed to predict system behavior and make real-time decisions regarding power distribution. The optimization framework incorporates factors such as PV production, battery state of charge (SoC), and grid emissions to achieve efficient energy utilization. The numerical analysis is developed considering a real load power profile of base stations, with variations of the PV capacity and the BESS capacity. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the EMS in reducing grid consumption, optimizing energy usage, and minimizing carbon emissions.

articleTitle: A Dynamic State Estimation Application for Stability and Uncertainty Mitigation in Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This work introduces a framework for frequency stability in smart grids based on dynamic state estimation. Real-time system conditions are tracked via PMU measurements which are then used to estimate and predict the frequency of the system. These estimates and predictions are produced through a modified version of the particle filter algorithm. Testing conducted via Matlab simulations shows that the proposed technique outperforms traditional and contemporary methods in terms of the amount of compensation used and by being able to produce an optimized response after a disturbance. Advantages of the particle filter over other Bayesian filters are also explored.

articleTitle: Mutual Induction Assessment in Hybrid AC/DC Transmission Lines – A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Converting one circuit of a double-circuit AC (Alternating Current) line to DC (Direct Current) is an attractive solution to increase the power transfer capacity of an existing electric corridor. One concern with such hybrid systems is the mutual electromagnetic induction between the two circuits, especially during asymmetric faults on the AC circuit when zero-sequence components arise. Previous works on the same topic do not focus on the analysis of harmonics produced by the interaction between the two systems. This paper presents the results obtained by a study of mutual interferences in a hybrid AC/DC transmission system during asymmetrical fault conditions. A hypothetical 400 kV AC - ±500 kV DC double-circuit line on the same tower is modelled in detail, and electromagnetic transient simulations have been performed using MATLAB/Simulink. The results highlight significant induced current components during faults, particularly if the AC circuit is not transposed.

articleTitle: An Innovative Methodology for Evaluating Power System Adequacy, Integrating Analyses of Both the Reliability and Anomalous Behaviour of Components
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Power systems adequacy assessment represents a complex task and many methodologies have been proposed to address its complexity. Different approaches have been investigated in literature: deterministic, probabilistic, analytical, analytical adaptive sampling approach, etc. The aim of this paper is proposing a probabilistic method combining both state sampling method and composite system analysis considering power system components reliability, reliability of power supply to electricity consumers, anomalous behaviour of the grid components, the presence of the non-programmable generation in the power system. Two case studies are analysed to show the proposed methodology effectiveness.

articleTitle: Real-Time Control of Renewable Community Energy Resources Including Demand Response Providers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This paper proposes a tool for the optimal real-time management of the resources of a renewable energy community. According to Italian Regulations, the renewable energy community members are fed by distribution networks connected to the upstream high-voltage network through the same substation. The community includes renewable energy systems, battery energy storage systems, and controllable and non-controllable loads. The proposed approach implements the optimal operation within a probabilistic framework and is aimed at maximising the community's shared energy, providing demand response to the distribution network, and providing available capacity for delivering services to the distribution grid and/or to the upstream grid. Numerical applications allow testing of the proposed real-time control tool showing its potential in terms of monitoring and control of the resources and of the required services.

articleTitle: HVDC Sea Electrodes: On the Choice of the Right Site
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The spreading diffusion of renewable energy leads to an increase in the transmission of electrical power using HVDC, which is more appropriate than HVAC to manage large quantities of less predictable power. Therefore, the number of main return electrodes, necessary to manage potential failures, will increase as well, making it more difficult to identify their suitable locations. This contribution is aimed at giving a clarification on the criteria that should be observed for correct electrode siting and arising related difficulties.

articleTitle: A Smart Large-Scale Synthesis of Na1.0Li0.2Ni0.25Mn0.75O2 as Cathode for Na-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Sodium-ion batteries (NIBs) represent one of the alternatives to lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), especially for large-scale energy storage. The interest in these batteries arises due to the intrinsic characteristics of sodium: it is cheap, abundant and, above all, environmentally friendly. Among the possible Na-based materials that could be used as cathode in NIBs, it was decided to investigate the performance of Na<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.0</inf>Li<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.25</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.75</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (NLNMO) spinel. NLNMO is a P2-type layered oxide and has attracted great attention as a cathode for NIBs. Despite its presenting some critical issues, especially regarding stability at high working voltage, it proved to be the most promising candidate among the materials belonging to this family. The activity carried out in the work envisaged the production of 1 kg of NLNMO suitable to be used as a cathode material in NIBs. The fundamental requirement was to obtain a high-quality material, at least equal to that synthesized on a laboratory scale. The most critical steps of the synthesis were studied for the possible scale-up step, namely the mixing of the reagents and the heating step. The laboratory scale synthesis was studied in terms of feasibility and scalability and the most critical points for a large-scale transition were analysed. In particular, the quantity of water to be added in the dissolution phase and the operating conditions of the heat treatment were optimized. To validate the performance of the NLNMO obtained on large-scale, it was used to prepare electrodes that were tested in battery. The electrochemical performances of these electrodes were then compared with those exhibited by the material prepared by laboratory-scale.

articleTitle: Design of Composites and Blends Based on Geopolymers for Heat Storage. Tests on Materials for Thermal Responses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: In order to develop innovative materials, technologies and systems for reducing CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>emissions in industrial applications, new geopolymeric materials, based on natural or wasted materials, with the best properties to build solid-state heat storage for medium temperatures, have been investigated. Heat could be recovered in industrial processes and re-used for other end-uses. Another possible use is storing heat in CSP plants with working fluid with temperatures up to 300 K, achieving performance better than cement-based concrete storage and easier than molten salts. The aim is to increase the durability of the materials for cyclic operation and high temperatures, increase conductivity and/or thermal capacity, optimal diffusivity values and environmental performance of solid-state storage systems in geopolymer concrete, exploiting recycled or waste raw materials, using local geomaterials.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Voltage Profile in Distribution Networks with High Penetration of Photovoltaic Energy Associated with Battery Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Clean energy sources, including Photovoltaic, in active distribution grids are bringing new challenges in terms of design and operation. An observed problem is the rising voltage profile in regions where PV generation is increasing. This paper proposes a model based on a Multi-period Optimal Power Flow (MOPF) for the placement and management of Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) in active distribution grids taking into account PV units. The model is implemented in AMPL, which is a Modelling language for Mathematical Programming, and deal with the Knitro solver for a 24-hour period aiming at minimizing the voltage deviations. Several experimental tests were carried out on a 33-Bus test system. The results demonstrate that the proposed model is effective in improving the voltage profile, e.g., in a case where the voltage exceeded its limit of 1.05 p.u. to 1.0726 p.u., utilizing the BESS returned it to the range (1.0324 p.u.). The results also indicate that the proposed model can enhance the performance of the power system, especially in terms of BESS placement.

articleTitle: The Impact of Climate Change on Ground Clearance and High Voltage Overhead Lines Discharge Risk
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The operation of overhead lines is strongly influenced by external environmental parameters such as solar radiation, ambient temperature, wind speed, and wind direction. Over the past few years, there has been a significant change in environmental conditions due to the increasingly evident climate change phenomenon, whose effects reduce average line ampacity; at the same time, the decarbonization process leads to an increased utilization of existing overhead lines. This paper aims to analyze the applicability of consolidated (20 years old) Italian standard within the ever-changing climatic context and determine whether the application of present-time conventional environmental conditions and line ratings still pose a discharge risk comparable to those foreseen in the standards. Data from distributed IoT monitoring systems, installed by Terna on HV and EHV are used to take into account the actual environmental conditions and line behaviour. More specifically, a real application on a EHV line in Sicily is taken into account, considering 10 different monitored line spans and a 2 years measurement period. The paper also investigates possible countermeasures for reducing the discharge risk while keeping the existing standard ampacity values for “hot period” and “cold period”.

articleTitle: Improvement of BLDC Motor Efficiency at Low Speed Operation through Internal Wiring Configuration Switching
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Nowadays, brushless direct current (BLDC) motors are widely used in transportation devices due to their light weight, to their reliability and durability, and also to their high efficiency. In this paper, a BLDC motor winding internal wiring configuration switching method is presented in order to achieve improved efficiency at the different torque-speed operating points. This method is particularly advantageous for low speed motor operation. The winding wiring is internally switched among different configurations, thus obtaining an equivalent coil with variable equivalent cross-section and number of turns. An experimental setup has been built with two identical machines mechanically coupled on the same shaft, the one with the original wiring configuration under generator or braking working regime, and the other with the proposed wiring configurations under motor working regime with its motor drive controller. Numerous tests have been performed under different controller setpoints and braking loads, satisfactorily achieving up to 30% motor power requirement reduction with respect to the original configuration.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicles Charging Stations Service Area Assessment Using Spatial Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The European Union (EU) has taken significant steps to lower CO2 emissions, with one of the key strategies being the promotion of electric vehicles (EVs) to reduce fossil fuel usage. A crucial aspect of this strategy is the accessibility of EV charging stations (CSs). In this study, we assess the service area of EVCSs in four European cities using spatial analysis tools in a GIS environment. Our aim is to compare the area and population coverage of EVCSs in three different Italian cities, namely Milan, Naples, and Palermo, to the European benchmark city in EV development, Amsterdam. The results showed that EVCS distribution is in excellent situation in Amsterdam with almost all citizens having access to at least one CS within 1 km distance. In the case of Italian cities, Milan has a better condition with almost covering 90 % of its population. However, other two cities, Naples and Palermo, are far from ideal situation with almost or below 50% coverages. The findings of this study will provide valuable insights into the current state and future potential of EV infrastructure in these cities.

articleTitle: Optimizing Wireless Power Transfer Systems for Improved Efficiency Through Geometric and Dimensional Alignments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Wireless Power Transfer Systems (WPTS) have emerged as a promising solution for Electric Vehicle (EV) charging, offering enhanced mobility and adaptability within microgrids. This paper proposes design considerations for ring and spiral circular coils in WPTS, addressing current issues and aiming for efficient EV charging. A detailed analytical estimation for inductive characteristics is provided for WPTS. Then, design optimization of the WPTS based on coil geometrical parameters and relative placement is proposed. COMSOL software is used to determine the inductive parameters accurately to validate theoretical analysis for our proposed 500W charging coils. Finally, the coupling coefficients of various coreless and cored charging pads are investigated with different geometric dimensions and coil alignments, with I-core being recommended to avoid bifurcation phenomena.

articleTitle: Smart Tests for Medium Voltage Cables in Renewable Energy Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The strong development of renewable power plants requires the installation of medium voltage underground cable networks which need to be tested with a pragmatic approach and with acceptable timing. This paper describes the tests to be carried out in the field on medium voltage cables before energization, providing rational explanations for each test.

articleTitle: Performance Based Sizing of Battery Energy Storage System for AC Shipboard Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Ensuring frequency stability is essential for the proper operation of a power system. Moreover, with the increasing electrification of ships driven by stringent emission regulations, the installation of batteries onboard ships is a major trend. While batteries traditionally serve as an energy resource to enhance efficiency, they also possess the potential to improve the performance in terms of voltage and frequency regulation. Therefore, this paper presents an optimal sizing methodology for Battery Energy Storage Systems considering their exploitation for Primary Frequency Regulation. The objective is to determine the optimal size of the BESS to ensure fast recovery time and contain frequency deviations after a perturbation.

articleTitle: Development of a New LED-Based Solar Simulator for Building-Integrated Photovoltaic Characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Building-Integrated Photovoltaics (BIPV) is an effective method of producing renewable energy providing also one or more functions of the building envelope. Among PV solutions, bifacial PV module technology captures sunlight from both the front and rear sides, increasing the module's power output per square meter. The evaluation of the overall performance of these cells is not easy because the irradiance conditions on the back side is variable. This article describes the design of a versatile light-emitting diode (LED) based solar simulator with independently controlled high-power LEDs. This laboratory-scale setup is designed to be suitable for the tests of bifacial cells reproducing the lighting conditions typical of the back side of the cells. To this aim an office configuration with bifacial PV glazing windows was simulated in DIALux to analyze the irradiance and lighting conditions on the glazing pane from inside environment. The results are used to choose the geometry features, the materials, and the operation mode of the lamps of the simulator.

articleTitle: Research on Corporate Decarbonization Planning Considering the Uncertainty of Procuring Renewable Energy Certificates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: In the context of the global decarbonization trend, decarbonization of the power sector is in the spotlight. Companies rely on purchasing renewable energy certificates (RECs) to decarbonize the electricity sector, so dealing with uncertainty in the price and regulation of RECs is a crucial challenge for companies working to decarbonize the electricity sector. This study aims to enable companies to develop power sector decarbonization plans considering the uncertainty in procuring RECs. To achieve this goal, we propose an algorithm continuously searching for decarbonization plans in each company's business site over time. We then propose a method to determine the number of RECs a company should procure, considering the uncertainty of the price of RECs. We further examine the impact of the inability to procure RECs and alternative solutions. In a case study, we demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed method using demand data from three factories of a major Japanese manufacturing company. The first value provided by this study is the development of an algorithm that incorporates company-wide decarbonization targets into site-specific decarbonization plans based on environmental changes and the characteristics of each site. The second is to propose a decarbonization approach considering the price and regulatory uncertainty of RECs procurement.

articleTitle: Exploiting the Energy Potential of Electric Vehicles for Improving the Reliability of Electricity Supply to the End User
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This article presents the possibility of using mobile electric energy storage to improve energy security for end users. Due to the ongoing energy transition and the increasing number of challenges regarding the need to keep the power system operating correctly on the one hand and the further promotion of the development of renewable energy sources on the other, it is necessary to consider whether the use of mobile energy storage facilities would solve some of them. The paper proposes how such a mobile energy storage should function and develops an example of the energy services it could provide. Based on actual data from the Warsaw University of Technology facility, it was also verified that it is possible to use such a solution to support power supply to the end user during unfavorable events occurring in the power system.

articleTitle: An Improved Method to Estimate PV Hosting Capacity for Distribution Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Integration of photovoltaic (PV) systems into low-voltage distribution grids presents numerous benefits including the reduction of fossil fuel dependency, mitigating carbon emissions, reducing line losses, curbing electricity demand during peak hours, and lowering generation costs. However, this integration also poses challenges such as grid stability, harmonic distortion, voltage surges, etc. To mitigate these issues, it is crucial to accurately determine the PV Hosting Capacity (PVHC) of a site, which signifies the maximum amount of PV that can be accommodated without causing over voltage for the considered distribution grid. This paper proposes an improved method utilizing a Python-based estimation algorithm that efficiently calculates the PV Hosting Capacity for a distribution grid driven by OpenDSS with a higher accuracy. An IEEE13-Bus Test Case is implemented within the OpenDSS environment, operating at 4.16 kV to evaluate the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Optimizing Renewable Energy Community Management Through Multi-Objective Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Multi-objective optimization plays a significant role in optimizing the sizing and operation of Renewable Energy Communities (RECs), facilitating informed decision-making through precise Pareto curves. In this study, we extend a model to incorporate thermal loads and explore the effectiveness of the A-AUGMECON2 algorithm and the Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) for solving it. Through comparative analysis, we aim to assess the performance and robustness of different optimization approaches in enhancing the sustainability and efficiency of REC operation.

articleTitle: A Profit Optimization Model for Renewable Energy Communities Based on the Distribution of Participants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: After the growth of decentralized system in the energy sector due to many benefits, a new concept of Renewable energy community (REC) in Europe is introduced. REC, which comprises local generation of renewable energy sources regulated by citizens, enterprises and Public Administrations, has emerged because of the growth of renewable sources in European Union countries. There are many benefits, including social, environmental and economical for making RECs and becoming part of it. However, this concept of RECs as per RED II has presented researchers with numerous research topics and opportunities. Among these, self-consumption, energy sold and energy sharing stand out as key concepts, enabling the optimization of renewable energy sources within these RECs. This work focuses on the mathematical model considering the optimization in REC to maximize profit based on the number of prosumers and consumers. In the model, the consumers could be part of REC and also could change their role from consumer to prosumer following the constraints set by regulatory. The optimization model is developed and analyzed on hourly basis as per Italian framework. Furthermore, this work also focuses on the economic analysis using different techniques to find the profitability at different cases for the optimal REC and without REC. Numerical results are obtained for different seasons and show that there is an optimal distribution of prosumers and consumers in which maximum profit can be obtained.

articleTitle: Optimal Self-Scheduling for Fast EV Charging Station on Highway: A Tunnel Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Highways are one of the main locations where installing an Electric Vehicle Charging Station (EVCS) is crucial. This paper introduces a novel concept to overcome the main challenge in this regard, which is the lack of enough electrical transmission systems close to the roads. The main idea is to leverage surplus power generated from nearby tunnels that have exclusive power supply. By capitalizing on excess power from the tunnel infrastructure, this study explores the feasibility of ultra-fast EVCSs facilities. The research investigates contingent upon the available power supply, with dual objectives: foremost, to optimize the accommodation capacity for EVs at the charging station, and secondly, to minimize the wait times for charging sessions. Employing advanced scheduling algorithms and mathematical optimization techniques, the study delineates optimal self-scheduling strategies for managing the charging infrastructure efficiently. This research contributes insights into the potential synergies of transportation infrastructure for the development of robust and efficient EVCSs along highways.

articleTitle: Clustering Spatiotemporal Wind Power for Resource Data Characterization and Potential Assessment in South Africa
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Integrating wind energy into an established electrical grid presents significant challenges due to its variability, necessitating robust grid integration strategies. Effective planning for integrating wind resources requires a thorough evaluation of resource characteristics and energy potential. This study utilizes clustering techniques on spatiotemporal wind power data in South Africa to support the country's efforts in incorporating wind power into its energy mix. The electricity grid in South Africa is considerably constrained due to inadequate infrastructure, limiting grid connection capacity. The research is focused on geographic regions within South Africa where connection capacity exists. Utilizing wind power data, which has been translated from speed data provided by the Wind Atlas for South Africa, the study aims to identify distinct clustered regions with varying characteristics that align with the national energy demand profile. K-means clustering, based on statistical features extracted from demand profiles, facilitates the identification of optimal sites and capacities for wind power plants. The research estimates the potential capacity for new wind generation, considering geographic, socioeconomic, and ecological factors, including grid capacity constraints. This method offers critical insights into resource adequacy and risk mitigation in energy planning,

articleTitle: Attenuation of Traveling Waves in HVDC Cable Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Propagation of travelling waves in HVDC cable systems, caused by events such as short circuits or abrupt earthing, is of great importance to understand whether cable accessories are adequately designed. The attenuation of travelling waves depends on cable materials and design. A relevant attenuation of high frequencies can be a desirable feature to damp fast transient events. In this paper a study is presented on attenuation of travelling waves carried out with a model that considers the frequency dependent properties of all the relevant cable materials. The model is applied both in the frequency and in the time domain and compared with typical models that neglect semi-conductive layers and water blocking tapes. Time domain transient analysis is carried out by means of Numerical Inverse Laplace Transform (NILT) method.

articleTitle: Real-Time System for Detection and Classification of Power Quality Disturbances
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Power quality is becoming a new global concern a result of integration of new technologies, the expansion of the smart grid and, increased penetration of renewables. This evolution of smart grids introduces new challenges and issues that affect the stability and reliability of the electrical grid. To successfully mitigate the consequences of power quality issues effectively, it is important to implement accurate real-time detection and classification. Despite the many models proposed for power quality classification, achieving real-time detection and classifying still remains a significant challenge. In this paper is presented a deep learning model for classification, evaluated using both synthetically generated and real data. The achieved results show great performance in classifying both types of data. Furthermore, a real-time system for detecting and classification of power quality disturbances is implemented and validated in a laboratory environment. The achieved results indicate that the model effectively classifies disturbances, thus contributing to improvements in real-time power quality.

articleTitle: Equipotential Bonding of Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The modules of photovoltaic systems (PV), whether land-mounted or installed on building roofs, are secured by racks and mounting structures. These components are usually constructed from metal, prompting the question of whether electrical bonding for equipotential reasons is necessary. Solar trackers may be employed in photovoltaic systems, equipped with servo motors that orient the payload toward the sun to maximize energy production. The servo may fail and energize the mounting structures. This paper advocates for bonding decisions to be based on the specific characteristics of the PV system and to be made on a case-by-case basis. The paper discusses the distinctions between Class I and Class II PV equipment, highlighting the implications for grounding and bonding based on the type of insulation employed. Through a detailed exploration of the underlying principles, design considerations, and industry standards, this paper endeavors to equip readers with the knowledge and tools necessary to make informed grounding decisions for their specific PV installations. It aims to contribute to the ongoing efforts toward safer, more efficient, and sustainable energy generation by addressing these critical aspects of PV systems design.

articleTitle: Electrical Engineers and the Infinity in Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: In the realm of power systems, infinity serves as a pivotal theoretical construct, facilitating the representation of extreme limits of quantities as they approach exceedingly large values. This theoretical framework simplifies complex problems and fosters creative problem-solving approaches for engineers. This paper explores the multifaceted role of infinity as a theoretical construct in power systems scenarios, showcasing how this abstraction harmonizes with the practical application of engineering principles. The discussion spans concepts such as the ground-potential and infinite bus as reference points, the significance of infinity in power lines analysis, the practical implications of short-circuits and open-circuits in power systems, and the continuity of state variables. By bridging the theoretical and practical aspects, this paper contributes to a comprehensive understanding of how infinity is harnessed as a tool in the field of electrical engineering, demonstrating its significance in simplifying intricate problems and advancing power systems design and analysis.

articleTitle: Correlation of OD Matrix and Traffic Volume with Functional Data Analysis: A Simulation-Based Case Study in the City of Portici
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This paper addresses the dynamic fluctuations within a single day of origin-destination (OD) flows and traffic volumes within urban networks, crucial for effective transportation planning and management. In an urban network, travel patterns are represented by two main variables: origin-destination (OD) flows and traffic volumes. The former (input of the assignment problem) are defined as the number of movements that occur between two points within the study area using transportation infrastructure, while the latter (output of the assignment problem) are defined as the number of vehicles crossing the transportation infrastructure within a given time interval. Traditional approaches encounter challenges due to the unobservability of OD flows and limitations in traffic data coverage and quality. Motivated by these limitations, we use a methodology based on functional data analysis with linear regression (FDA-1r), which enables the exploration of functional relationships between predictor (OD flow) and response (link volume). We present a case study in Portici, Italy, utilizing the FDA-1r methodology to analyze the correlation between OD flows and link flows. Results demonstrate the efficacy of the method in modeling the relationship between OD flows and link flows, providing valuable insights for urban traffic management. This paper contributes to advancing Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) services by addressing real-time OD matrix correction challenges.

articleTitle: A Computerized Multimodal Gallery for the Smart Management of Human Emotions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: In this work a multimodal gallery was developed, from which to extract positive stimuli that reduce people stress level. Positive and negative stimuli were selected from IAPS, IADS, and E-MOVIE databases and were separately evaluated by two groups of forty-four participants using PANAS and SAM questionnaires. The effect of the stimulations on mood induction was assessed using a mixed-model analysis of variance (ANOVA) Group (positive, negative) x Time (pre, post). Experimental results indicated that images and movies were effective in managing human emotions, producing a significant difference in participants emotional state after their presentation respect to baseline; sounds did not result able to affect the emotional states of participants. Basing on the experimental results a multimodal gallery was developed: it is composed of positive images and videos; also sounds were included as neutral stimuli.

articleTitle: Improving Very Short-Term Wind Power Predictability by Strategically Placing Weather Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This study aims to improve the accuracy of wind power generation forecasting by selecting the potential locations for weather stations, which serve as crucial data sources for wind predictions. The proposed method is based on using Shapley values. First, they are assigned to stations that are already available in the region based on their contribution to forecasting error. Second, the values are interpolated to cover the area of interest. We test the hypothesis that taking weather measurements in areas with negative Shapley values leads to a decrease in the error of forecasting the volume of wind power generation. We estimate the method's impact on forecasting error by using long short-term memory neural network and linear regression with quadratic penalization. The results of this proof-of-concept study indicate that it is possible to improve the short-term wind power forecasts using additional weather observations in the selected regions. The future research should be dedicated to the expansion of the case study area to other locations, including offshore power plants.

articleTitle: Parameter Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries Using GSKPSO Hybrid Method Based on Impedance Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid method to estimate lithium-ion (Li-ion) battery model parameters based on impedance data is proposed. Gaining-sharing knowledge (GSK) is combined with particle swarm optimization (PSO) to take advantage of the exploration and exploitation mechanisms of both algorithms. The main contribution is a robust method capable of determining with high reliability (standard deviation of magnitude 1E-16) the parameters of Li-ion batteries requiring a low computational cost.

articleTitle: Time-of-Use Electricity Utilization for EV Charging Through Smart Systems with Battery Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Electric vehicles become increasingly prevalent in recent years speeding up the peak demand, grid overloading, the need for distribution system modifications, voltage fluctuations, and grid congestion. Efficient, innovative, and ecological charging methods are needed to address these issues. Smart charging systems with demand-side management methodologies present a promising chance to tackle these difficulties. This study presents a technique for enhancing the utilization of time- of-use electricity when charging electric vehicles, especially in integrating additional battery storage in smart charging systems. The goal is to reduce both charging costs and the strain on the power grid. An advanced charging system has been developed to charge electric vehicles, considering factors including time-of- use electricity prices, the state of charge of additional battery storage, and the electric vehicle. A detailed model has been developed with MATLAB/Simulink. The study's outcomes offer valuable insights into the advantages and viability of integrating additional battery storage into a smart charging infrastructure. Through the optimization of time-of-use electricity consumption for EV charging, owners can reduce their electricity costs while contributing to a more sustainable and resilient energy environment.

articleTitle: Supercapacitor Characterization Over a Wide Current Range
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Supercapacitors offer distinct advantages over traditional batteries or other energy storage systems, such as high-power density and extended lifecycle. However, it is crucial to accurately model their behavior under various operating conditions, especially at high currents exceeding hundreds of amperes. This study explores the effectiveness of an equivalent model, previously introduced in the literature, but extends its testing range from 20 A up to the nominal current of the devices (140 A) in continuous mode. The tests are performed on large commercial supercapacitor cells contributing to a deeper understanding of supercapacitor performance in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Deep Analysis of Quasi-MPPT Hysteresis Control for Multiple Energy Sources in Low-Power Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Thermoelectric generators (TEGs) are capable of producing electrical energy through energy conversion from thermal energy based on the Seebeck Effect and have proven to be very useful in small-scale applications, especially through the valorization of waste heat. However, these applications may demand a higher power than a single TEG can provide. Therefore, to compensate for this demand, multiple TEGs can be electrically connected to form an array. While there are benefits using an array of TEGs, there are also many aspects to consider. One major aspect is how to compensate for the potential of temperature mismatch within the array. If not suitably managed, this could significantly complicate the control as well as the maximum power tracking (MPPT) performance as all the TEGs will not be operating at their maximum power points. Potential electronic interfaces that may be suitable to compensate for this mismatch will be examined and discussed. After this analysis, an optimal electronic interface will be proposed and a detailed analysis regarding its operation will be carried out.

articleTitle: Non-linear Control of PEM Electrolyzers in DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Ahstract- The energy transition has led to an increase in the implementation of renewable energy sources. Along with this increase, two technologies have gathered interest. These are DC microgrids and proton exchange membrane electrolyzers. DC microgrids provide simplified control and lower conversion losses. Meanwhile, electrolyzers produce hydrogen that helps maximize the use of renewable energy sources while providing long-term storage. This work seeks to study the coordination of such electrolyzers with other elements in DC microgrids. Non- linear droop controls are proposed to ensure the coordination of the electrolyzers with other energy storage devices such as batteries. A DC microgrid along with the electrolyzer is implemented in MATLAB/Simulink. The results show that the proposed controller allows a seamless transition to a standby state while allowing it to complement the battery in the DC microgrid.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Networks for Identifying Modes of Transport Using GPS Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The use of GPS-based data collection methods has gradually replaced traditional survey-based methods in recent years as a result of the ability to extract more accurate trip data from mobile devices like smartphones. Inferring travel modes is essential to understand passengers' travel behavior and various machine and deep learning techniques have shown their ability to extract valuable details from GPS data. In this study, we introduce a convolutional neural network to extract high-level features from GPS data to recognize transport modes of trips. After preprocessing the raw GPS data to compute motion and displacement characteristics, is sliced into fixed-sized segments. Then, a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is used to train a model able to detect five transport modes. Our model improved the final accuracy of test data by 2.84% and outperformed previous work in predicting transit mode.

articleTitle: Multi-Horizon Energy Markets: Optimization of Resilient Operational Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This paper proposes an optimal day-ahead resilient commitment model for multi-carrier energy systems (MCESs) that participate in multiple energy markets. In the proposed model, the electricity, heating, and cooling sectors are considered. Moreover, the model comprises multiple distributed energy resource aggregators. The proposed model optimizes the MCES's operation by minimizing its operation costs within a multi-carrier energy system framework. This study makes a significant contribution by proposing a multi-stage robust optimization model for energy markets that utilizes preventive and corrective measures in both the day-ahead and real-time horizons. The simulation results show that the proposed method in this paper reduces expected costs by 44.31% compared to the base case.

articleTitle: Prominent Progress in Polysulfone-Based Anion Exchange Membrane Fabrication by Electrospinning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Developing cost-effective anion exchange membranes (AEMs) with boosted ionic conductivity, desired mechanical properties, and sufficient alkaline stability remains a significant challenge in manufacturing. We've made great progress in producing an intrinsic AEM by electrospinning with a blended polymeric solution of polysulphone and Fumion®FAA-3 (a commercial anion exchange ionomer solution from Fuma-Tech, Germany), followed by characterization tailored for water electrolyzer applications. Our results demonstrate significant potential for propelling the manufacturing of a novel breed of electrospun AEMs optimized for hydrogen production. The outcome represents a prominent improvement over our initial endeavor, which is a big step forward in our goal to make manufacturing easier and create top-notch AEMs for hydrogen production.

articleTitle: First Step in Real-Time Energy Management: Forecasting Energy Production Using Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The industrial revolution has led to a rise in energy needs and the demand for better control strategies. Intelligent Energy Management Systems (IEMS) and the Internet of Energy (IoE) offer promising solutions to cut down energy usage in the construction industry. This paper looks at the first step before combining these ideas to address challenges in energy management which is the prediction of the source's power, particularly around non-linear functions and choosing energy sources. The study compares three machine learning models K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting - using a solar power generation dataset. Results show that the Random Forest model performs better than the others in predicting power generation patterns, demonstrating robust performance. However, the limitations of the Gradient Boosting and KNN models highlight the importance of selecting appropriate models tailored to specific tasks. Overall, this research provides insights to enhance energy management systems for improved efficiency and cost-effectiveness.

articleTitle: Enhancing Short-Term Energy Forecasting in Distributed Systems Through Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Energy consumption forecasting plays an important role in smart buildings, enabling energy monitoring, and planning. Especially nowadays it is a useful tool that can alert the consumers for upcoming energy usage peaks. In the literature, there is a gap in energy usage forecasting for educational institutions. They are suitable study cases because they are research centers that develop and create novel concepts and serve as examples for energy-efficient buildings. This paper proposes an approach for short-term energy consumption forecasting for buildings that are property of Ss Cyril and Methodius University in Skopje. The proposed model is trained on 25 different university department buildings' data from January 1, 2021 to November 16, 2023, with a resolution of one hour without threatening data privacy. Energy usage and positional encoding of hour, day of week, and month are used as input variables. The proposed approach utilizes federated learning technique to develop a generalized deep learning model for short-term forecasts. Additionally, a comparison between recurrent neural networks in centralized and decentralized learning approach is presented. The model performance is evaluated using the following metrics: RMSE and MAE. The obtained results show that federated learning achieves great performance.

articleTitle: Smart Grid Solution for Fast Power System Balancing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Increasing the production of renewable energy sources has become an important goal in the power energy sector in European Union. At the same time, volatile nature of wind, solar, and unplanned outages causes congestion and imbalances in power system operation. To compensate for these deviations from the normal state, transmission system operators have different market management mechanisms. Secondary and tertiary load frequency control or imbalance cooperation can be used within contracted ranges. In practice, there are often situations in which they are not sufficient to level the deviations. In such situations, the only available measure is the curtailment of renewable energy. Transmission system operators are challenged to preserve the security of the power system and allow renewable production as much as possible under many different operating conditions. An algorithm for curtailment of renewable power plants and fast execution of set points is developed within the Croatian transmission system and will be presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle Flexibility Harnessing Through Local Energy Community Operation Optimization: Maximizing Local Energy Utilization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: With an uprising penetration, local energy communities (LECs) face the local challenge of reaching energy self-sufficiency (catering for high generation-demand time mismatch) and the system-wide challenge of securely operating within the distribution network. In this sense, a novel strategy for LEC operation is proposed to overcome these challenges, aiming to maximize local consumption by controlling the charging/discharging of EVs and exploiting distributed generation resources at full, guaranteeing a distribution system secure operation. For this, the local operation of LECs (encompassing conventional and flexible demand members and prosumer members) is represented by a mixed-integer linear programming model, also considering the LEC interaction with the distribution network, and distribution system technical limits. To validate the proposed strategy, the impact of the economic interaction among LECs as well as EV charging/discharging control on LECs’ self-consumption, was analyzed in a case study under different operation conditions. The numerical results demonstrate that, when compared to the baseline scenario, EV charging/discharging coordination enabled the local supply of 80.5% of the LECs' daily energy, increasing to 88.31% when the interaction between LECs is enabled.

articleTitle: Mid-Term Feasibility Assessment of Battery Electric Trucks and Fuel Cell Electric Trucks
