publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Decarbonization policies in the transportation and mobility sector increasingly require studies and evaluations to quantify the possible benefits of alternatives to current solutions. In addition to passenger transport, studies are also underway in freight transport to assess the feasibility of using electric or hydrogen-powered road vehicles. In this context, the goal of this paper is to evaluate the feasibility of using battery- or hydrogen-powered trucks (grey, blue and green) to replace current diesel-powered vehicles. Specifically, three types of journeys are assumed: short, repetitive and long hauls. For each journey type, two-time horizons are considered: current situation and year 2030 (pessimistic and optimistic scenario). For each alternative (battery and hydrogen), the analysis involves the identification of 6 KPIs (Truck cost, Truck Maintenance, Payload, Fuel/Energy cost, Refuel, Emission) that allow an index to be determined through the use of relative importance weights.

articleTitle: A Frequency Stability Scheme Based on Dynamic Estimation and Spectral Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Modern frequency stability schemes are static and reactive. They are based on fixed settings and they do not consider the dynamic nature of the grid. These schemes operate only after the system enters a critical state. This work proposes a proactive approach based on the particle filter and spectral clustering. Future frequency values are estimated through the particle filter. This makes it possible to generate an optimized response. This optimization includes establishing areas for distributed control using dynamic system data via spectral clustering. The performance of the concept is evaluated via Matlab simulations using IEEE test systems. The results show that the technique proposed was able to stabilize the test system in the aftermath of a disturbance while providing optimized corrective actions.

articleTitle: Dynamic Interactions of a High-Current Thyristor-Rectifier Interfaced PEM Electrolyzer with the Angular Dynamics of Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The increasing presence of power electronic converter interfaced loads, such as hydrogen proton exchange membrane electrolyzers (PEMEL), has caused a notable shift in the dynamics of the power system. Thus, it is of interest to analyze the dynamic response of synchronous generators (SGs) when high-current converters interfaced PEMEL are connected close to them. This paper investigates the dynamic interactions of a large current thyristor-rectifier interfaced PEMEL with the rotor angle transient stability. First, the paper investigates if a large PEMEL can be modeled as a load composed of fractions of constant impedance, constant power, or constant current. Thus, the dynamic electrochemical model of the PEMEL and the current control structure for a 12-pulse thyristor rectifier are defined. Afterward, the effect on the rotor angle transient stability is studied. The PEMEL model and the current control structure proposed are tested in the Belgian power system. Time-domain simulations are used to assess this effect using Matlab/Simscape. The obtained results show that the thyristor-rectifier interfaced with 100 MW of PEMEL enhances the dynamic response of the SGs under large disturbances by increasing the maximum fault-clearing time. The dynamic interactions of the PEMEL with the angular dynamics of SGs depend on the number of PEMELs connected in parallel to the busbar close to the SGs.

articleTitle: Conversion of Wind Power Plants to Hybrid Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: In recent years, the energy transition has imposed a diversity of energy generation sources on electrical systems, significantly expanding the role of renewable energy sources such as solar, wind, and hydroelectric power. However, the intermittent nature of these sources, reliant on external factors, poses challenges to their efficient integration into the grid. Consequently, there is often underutilization of the infrastructure installed for energy transmission. This research aims to address this challenge by evaluating the technical feasibility of repurposing existing wind power plants into hybrid facilities. By combining different energy sources at a single location, hybrid plants can potentially mitigate the intermittency issues associated with individual renewable sources. The proposed methodology involves the analysis of operational projects in Brazil, assessing their capacity for integrating complementary energy sources. Through this evaluation, this work seeks to identify opportunities for optimizing resource utilization and enhancing the overall efficiency of energy infrastructure. The findings reveal significant potential for the development of hybrid plants, indicating a promising avenue for maximizing renewable energy utilization and ensuring a more resilient and sustainable energy grid.

articleTitle: Designing a Platform for Energy Recovery and Monitoring in Building Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Energy efficiency measures are pivotal in addressing the high energy consumption and gas emissions of the building sector. Moreover, increasing attention is given to indoor environmental quality to ensure comfort and healthy conditions for the occupants. Sustainable and energy-efficient solutions are needed to avoid the extensive use of battery-based wireless network sensors. In this work, a platform has been conceived and designed to recover unused indoor energy sources and convert them into useful power for environmental sensors to monitor buildings. A preliminary energy analysis of the main components of such a platform has been carried out to demonstrate the feasibility of the system.

articleTitle: Ground Fault Detection Method for Electric Systems with Partial Power Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Partial power converters (PPCs) have demonstrated to be efficient, high-density and reduced electrical stress solutions. However, due to their lack of maturity, PPCs still require an extensive analysis on their reliability. This paper presents a ground fault detection method for PPC-based solutions. The approach relies on a grounding resistor that is sequentially linked between the positive, negative, and midpoint terminals of the DC systems, grounded by three distinct switches. Through the article, the method and the necessary components are described in detail. Later, the simulation set-up (carried out in a MATLAB-Simulink) and its results are shown. The results conclude that this method not only detects the fault, but also its location, saving time and money.

articleTitle: Enhancing SME Energy Management: Development of an Assessment Tool to Identify Improvement Opportunities and Support their Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: To address the gap in energy management tools tailored specifically for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), this paper discusses a research project aimed at developing an assessment tool to evaluate and improve energy management practices within this critical economic group. The methodology presented includes a thorough literature review focused also on principles from the ISO 50001 family of international technical standards to ensure that the tool meets global best practices in energy management. The resulting maturity model will aim to help SMEs to perform comprehensive self-assessments, helping to identify strengths and weaknesses in their energy management practices. The tool is designed to be user-friendly and provide immediate feedback to help identify and address areas for improvement. The expected outcomes include enhanced energy management, increased efficiency, and the collection of relevant information about the general state of energy management in SMEs. We anticipate that the tool will provide helpful support to SMEs in understanding their energy management needs and in starting a practical and solid improvement plan.

articleTitle: Diffusion Models: an Application to Evaluate the Spread of Electric Vehicle on the City of Salerno (South of Italy)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The use of Electric Vehicles (EVs) could be one of the possible solutions for reducing emissions due to the higher energy efficiency on board and the possibility of recharge vehicles with energy produced by renew ables sources. Different methodologies are available in the literature for assessing the spread of EVs and among these, diffusion models are also beginning to being explored in this field. Few studies, however, are available to represent the evolution of EVs diffusion phenomena in Italy. This study focuses on the EVs spread in Italy, providing a specific analysis using the Bass standard model. Moreover, a sensitivity analysis on the innovation and imitation parameters has been carried out to analyze different possible scenarios and to highlight initiatives that can speed up the spread of EVs. Additionally, adopting the same methodology a case study is then carried out on the city of Salerno (south of Italy). Results obtained for Salerno are compared with the major Italian cities: Milan, Rome and Naples. Finally, with the help of macro-simulation software a zoning of Salerno is performed and a specific analysis of the EVs spread on each macrozone is reported using Bass Standard model.

articleTitle: A Novel Topology for High Voltage Battery Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel topology for high voltage battery energy storage systems (BESS), addressing the challenge of achieving necessary power and voltage for effective energy storage without exposing cells to harmful high voltages stress. Such exposure risks accelerated degradation and electrical faults. This research presents a scalable and simple solution using high frequency power transformers (HFPT) in a cascade configuration, allowing the use of low voltage cells in high voltage applications and avoiding the issues common to traditional series-parallel cell setups. The key advantages of the proposed topology include its simplicity, scalability, and ability to significantly reduce voltage stress, thereby enhancing system efficiency and reliability. Simulation results from MATLAB-Simulink support the effectiveness of the presented topology, suggesting its potential to improve high voltage battery storage systems.

articleTitle: Study of the Influence of the Motion Limit of a Horizontal Single-Axis Tracker on the Annual Incident Energy in a PV Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This paper analyses the influence of the motion limit of a horizontal single-axis tracker on the incident energy on the PV field. The Miraflores PV power plant (Spain) is analysed. As most of the PV power plants in Spain have a motion limit of ±60 (<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup>) (so-called actual scenario). A Mathematica© code has been implemented to calculate the annual incident energy and the daily incident energy in the PV field. The proposed assessment indicator is the annual incident energy ratio with respect to the actual scenario. The maximum annual incident energy corresponds to the actual scenario, but the reduction of the motion limit does not imply excessive energy losses. For ß<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> = ±55(<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup>) this loss is 0.050%. The ß<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> = ±55(<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup>) scenario slightly favours the diffuse component and the actual scenario favours the beam component. Therefore, at a location where the diffuse component predominates, the actual scenario may not be optimal.

articleTitle: Microfrontend Application for Microgrids Monitoring and Controling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The idea of microgrids has been settled as a transformative solution for the future of energy, promising enhanced resilience, sustainability, and efficiency in the distribution. management and consumption of electricity. These localized grids operate autonomously from the traditional wide-area synchronous grid and are capable of balancing loads through the intelligent integration of renewable resources, energy storages, and responsive demand programs. In parallel, the development of Internet technologies has fostered the development of advanced Internet applications adapted to streamline complex system interactions through user-friendly interfaces. The coupling of these two domains introduces the innovative concept of microfrontend applications for microgrids, aiming to improve efficiency of the monitoring and operation of these units in power systems.

articleTitle: Determining the Likely Tracking Choices for Utility Scale Photovoltaic Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: During long-term generation capacity expansion planning, generalised solar photovoltaic (PV) power generation profiles are used to represent expected future production. These profiles should ideally capture the varying solar resource characteristics across the region under consideration, as well as account for likely future PV technology choices (e.g. singleversus bi-facial) and orientation decisions (e.g. single-axis versus dual-axis tracking versus fixed). This paper investigates the hypothesis that the PV power generation profile used in South Africa”s recent long-term planning simulations does not accurately represent the current and expected future PV power generation in the country. The hypothesis is tested through a literature review and industry interviews aimed at determining the cost drivers and financial viability of various technology and orientation scenarios in South Africa's future generation capacity, ultimately informing the expected future contribution of PV and the expected representative power profile for current and future PV plants. The results highlight a significant disparity between the predominant use of fixed-tilt orientation systems in recent long-term planning, and the shift towards tracking solutions as indicated by this research. The techno-economic simulations clearly demonstrated monofacial (rather than bi-facial) single-axis tracking as the most cost-effective solution, with fixed-tilt solutions not optimal in any of the scenarios simulated. The paper contributes by showing that the current PV power profile used in South Africa”s long-term planning is not representative of the actual current and future PV technology and orientation choices. A second contribution is the establishment of a new profile that does represent these current and likely future choices. These results will be valuable to modellers and planners active in planning South Africa”s future power system.

articleTitle: Detecting Abnormal Profiles in a PV Power Plant Data Using Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This paper presents a novel concept for abnormal profile detection in PV plants, leveraging advanced data analytics techniques. Unlike conventional methods, which primarily rely on periodic data readings, our approach emphasizes continuous monitoring and comparative analysis of multiple parameters. By integrating machine learning algorithms, specifically tailored for PV systems, we propose a dynamic framework capable of identifying deviations from expected operational patterns in real-time. This framework not only enhances fault detection capabilities but also facilitates predictive maintenance strategies, thereby maximizing plant reliability and performance. Through rigorous testing and validation on diverse PV installations, our methodology demonstrates robustness and scalability, offering a promising solution for the sustainable management of PV assets in the evolving energy landscape.

articleTitle: A Triple-Active Bridge Based Solid State Transformer Fast Charging Station Topology For Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: There is a recent trend in Electric Vehicle (EV) batteries to shift to 800-V range battery electric vehicle standard instead of the conventional 400-V range standard. Separate chargers would be required to support each EV battery standard. This paper proposes a Triple-Active Bridge-based Solid-State transformer charger topology. This topology allows the charging station to support the two standards using fewer components and higher power densities. The TAB-based SST also has controlled bidirectional power flow among its ports, which allows Grid to Vehicle (G2V) and Vehicle to Grid (V2G) operations. The study introduces the power flow decoupling and a systematic design procedure for the fast charger topology to support both standards. The effectiveness of the charger topology is verified through simulation using MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electric Arc Furnace Influence on Power Quality in Low and Medium Voltage Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This paper focuses on analyzing power quality issues resulting from electric arc furnace operation. It highlights the challenges posed by the stochastic nature of the arc and proposes strategies to mitigate its impact on the power grid. Through measurements carried out on the medium and low voltage side of the furnace, fluctuations in parameters such as voltage, current, and power factor were observed, indicating significant disturbances in power quality. Mitigation strategies, including e.g. installing compensators, are suggested to stabilize the network and improve power quality, enhancing efficiency and reducing energy consumption and electrode usage.

articleTitle: Influence of the Experimental Setup on the Shielding Performance of Perforated Grids Against an Indirect Electrostatic Discharge
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Experimental validation is often looked for to corroborate numerical or analytical formulations. However, in shielding problems, a number of issues should be carefully considered before comparing the results ensuing from a measurement campaign with those attained analytically or numerically. In this manuscript the typical configuration of perforated shield is considered against a source of electrostatic discharge, putting in evidence the most relevant aspects influencing the experimental results, either from a qualitative and quantitative point of view.

articleTitle: Knowledge-Discovery-Based Methods for Wind Power Generators Performance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Wind power generator performance monitoring is essential to maximize wind energy conversion. Based on this, in the present work, a novel multi-step methodology is formulated for identifying the status of operating wind turbines. At first, the monthly power profiles of each wind turbine in a farm are computed and elaborated to highlight possible performance deterioration, and the wind farm is divided into potentially anomalous and presumably not anomalous wind power generators. Then, innovative data-driven methods are formulated to inquire if the potential anomaly is real or is only apparent (due, for example, to defective sensors). Two separate Machine Learning (ML) regression models predict the intensity of the wind and the power produced by each wind generator suspected of being anomalous, relative to the quantities measured at the surrounding machines. By analyzing the statistical properties of the difference between the predicted and the actual values, it is possible to identify if the potentially anomalous wind turbines are indeed performing correctly or not. One year of data from ten industrial multi-MW aerogenerators are analyzed. One wind turbine is shown to be affected by an anemometer defective sensor and it is argued that there are no associated producible power losses. Thus, the collected evidences prove the goodness of the formulated method and highlight the importance of advanced data analysis methods for a correct interpretation of wind power generators' operation.

articleTitle: Assessment of the Electrostatic Field Uniformity Within an Electrospinning Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The analysis carried out made it possible to evaluate the electrostatic field in an electrospinning device by means of a Comsol finite element model. The study focuses on the main factors affecting the generation of nanofibers and on the uniformity of the electrostatic field over the collector. In particular, the behaviour of the electrostatic field vector close to the needle and along the edges of the collector was assessed. Finally, the electric field at several points on the collector surface was computed in Comsol. The obtained data were processed in Matlab to assess the variation of the electric field along the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex>; -and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$y$</tex> -directions. The model results allow to explain interesting aspects arising from the use of the machine.

articleTitle: New Design of Multilayer Microwave Absorbing Structures Using Ceramic/CNT Slabs for X-Band Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: In this study, the optimization approach has been applied to enhance the design of multilayered microwave-absorbing structures. The optimization method is based on choosing parameters such as layers arrangement, layers thickness, absorption index, and shielding effectiveness (SE). The main purpose of this investigation is to find the optimal structure with high absorption and shielding effectiveness. This method is applied on a new multilayered structures based on Conductive Layers (CLs) of Carbon Nanotube (CNT) with ceramic layers of zirconium dioxide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{ZrO}_{2})$</tex>. The performance of the structure is evaluated in the X-band frequency range. The simulation results showed that the design of the obtained structure has better absorption index picks <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(> 90\%)$</tex> and low magnitude value <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{11}$</tex> with small layer thickness. This approach is interesting for future works focusing on highlighting the efficient microwave absorbing and shielding (MA&S) structures with high electromagnetic performances suitable for X-band applications.

articleTitle: EV Charger Introduction Planning for Airport Parking Utilizing Surplus Energy of Daytime Solar Panel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Introducing electric vehicle (EV) chargers to the renewable energy used facilities is beneficial for both EV users and facilities. However, there are some obstacles to introduce them. For EV users, they tend to be anxious about availability of charger because of few amounts of EV chargers. On the other hand, for facilities, they have no idea actual charging demand and how many chargers to be installed under multiple objectives. In this study, we propose the method to determine the number of chargers in the facilities considering multiple objectives such as cost, sustainability and charging demand. Our approach defines three objective functions, and through these outputs, the optimal combination of chargers is determined using Pareto front. Finally, we create a roadmap for the number of chargers according to several prepared scenarios. One of the new aspects of this study compared to existing research is considering the elements of Vehicle-to-Building(V2B). While our study has some limitations, such as assuming all users charge their EVs full at home and not changing dischargeable chargers' price in the future, the quantitative method for determining the number of chargers considering multiple objectives is important for the facility's decision-making.

articleTitle: Utilizing P-median and Machine Learning for Bike-Sharing Demand Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Bike-sharing systems (BSS) are under careful examination for their potential to improve urban accessibility and sustainable transportation. Despite their widespread adoption, effectively managing BSS encounters difficulties arising from imbalances between demand and supply. The key challenge in BSS operation is accurately forecasting bike demand across different stations. The task was addressed in this paper through regression techniques such as Random Forest (RF), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Regularized Linear Regression (Ridge), and Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) for short-term predictions. n this study, we utilize comprehensive datasets encompassing bicycle-sharing activities and weather conditions in Los Angeles. Integrating these datasets with the p-median method for station grouping, we examine the delicate balance between median values and prediction accuracy. Furthermore, our investigation reveals that among the various models scrutinized, RF and XGBoost consistently exhibit superior performance.

articleTitle: Improving Dynamic Response of Hydro Power Plants Using Electrical Energy Storage in Low-inertia Power Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The share of renewable energies in the electricity generation side is increasing to replace fossil fuels and address environmental concerns. Consequently, the total rotational mass of conventional generations and the inertia of the power system will decrease. Here, first the potential of hydro power plant assisting the power system operator managing frequency deviations, in a low inertia power system is studied. Then, the capability of electrical energy storage (EES) to assist hydro power plant in primary frequency response services, is surveyed. The droop control method is considered for the operation of EES facility, with values of 1 and 5. Different case studies are defined, to study the impact of the hydro power plant and the EES facility on primary frequency response of the system. Based on the results, the hydro power plant will improve the settling time, and final recovered value of frequency of the system after a disturbance. However, it has a rather slow dynamic response facing deviations in the power system frequency. The EES facility has the best improvement in the Nadir point, while the settling point is better than when the system is without hydro power plant. Moreover, the final value of the frequency after a disturbance is also higher than the case without hydro power plant and EES facility. Finally, the droop control with value of 5 has better performance than droop with value of 1.

articleTitle: The Effect of a Bifacial PV-Based Glazed Facade Applied to an Office Building: Analysis of the Electricity Energy Balance by Means of Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: New technologies based on photovoltaic devices integrated into windows as active elements exhibit high potential for achieving a significant increase in the energy produced from renewable energy sources (RES), even in urban areas. The building sector has a considerable impact on emissions in the city environment. This work analyses the potential of building integrated photovoltaic systems (BIPVs) by simulating the installation of a bifacial photovoltaic glazed façade for an office building in two Italian cities. The same building is simulated in two different Italian cities, Perugia (PG) and Catania (CT), through EnergyPlus dynamic simulation program. The resulting datasets are used to train a neural network which predicts the energy demand for cooling and heating required to maintain comfortable indoor temperatures. Additionally, bifacial PV-based glazed façades are appropriately simulated for the calculation of the hourly energy balance during winter and summer seasons. Finally, the environmental benefits obtained through the usage of the PV-glazing system are analysed.

articleTitle: Non-Intrusive Measurement of Two-Port Impedance Parameters by Clamp-on Inductive Probes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Many applications in the field of power electronics benefit from in-circuit impedance measurements, including modelling of electromagnetic interference and stability analysis of control systems. Noteworthy, a non-intrusive characterization of a system can be obtained, in real operating condition, by clamp-on inductive probes. Unfortunately, the characterization of a multiport system requires the measurement of an impedance matrix, which cannot be obtained by currently known one-port in-circuit impedance measurement techniques. Recently, the introduction of a novel inductively coupled technique allowed non-intrusive measurements of admittance matrices. Though the impedance matrix can be found by inversion of the admittance matrix, this operation is subject to numerical errors. Hence, an alternative formulation allowing direct measurement of impedance parameters is presented in this paper. The proposed method is validated using one set of passive networks, and comparing results with those obtained by direct measurement from a vector network analyser, showing good accuracy from 150 kHz to 30 MHz.

articleTitle: Optimizing Integrated Shading Device and Light Shelf for Daylight Performance and Visual Comfort in Architecture Studio
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: To provide a sustainable interior, it is essential to consider visual comfort and energy efficiency for the occupants' well-being. Daylight is crucial in providing visual comfort while proposing energy-efficient design alternatives. Using daylight as a primary source is one of the most crucial strategies. However, controlling daylight for unwanted situations such as discomfort glare is important. There have been several research studies on daylighting, visual comfort, and shading techniques. Shading devices are façade configurations to control daylight, while light shelves distribute daylight evenly through the space. There are two types of classifications for shading devices: adaptive ones and non-adaptive ones. Numerous research studies have been conducted on daylighting, energy consumption, occupancy performance, and shading systems. Shading technologies, whether adaptive or not, provide benefits and drawbacks. Even though optimizing them is one way to design non-adaptive shading devices, they require minimal maintenance. This study aims to integrate adaptive shading devices and light shelves for university campus buildings to provide lighting design strategies. The aim is to create a study environment that promotes well-being and academic achievement. To pursue this study, three optimization algorithms were run to find the nearly optimal solution. The goal was to both maximize Daylight Autonomy and uniformity values. Results showed that HypE and SPEA2 results discovered near-optimal DA above 75% and uniformity between 0.6 and 0.7.

articleTitle: Unlocking Demand Response Potentials by Electric Vehicle Charging Stations in Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Increasing the number of Electric Vehicles (EVs) imposes several challenges in power distribution networks. Developed Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE) provides fast and efficient charging of EVs at the Public Charging Stations (PCS). These chargers benefit from balanced three-phase chargers with considerable power consumption. Hence, the optimal management and task scheduling for EVSE should be arranged in such a way as to avoid overloading network infrastructure or imposing new peaks on the distribution networks. On the other hand, energy management in the presence of high renewable energy penetration due to installed Photovoltaic (PV) panels at the low-voltage (LV) distribution network should be elaborated to minimize the renewable power curtailment. Hence, this paper presents a novel model to address the optimal scheduling of charging stations availability and unlocking the Demand Response (DR) potentials at the distribution networks with highly penetrated PV panels. The energy management model is represented as a standard Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) problem which can be solved by open-source solvers. The proposed model is tested for a real case study in Portugal to demonstrate the functionality of the developed tool.

articleTitle: Battery-Less Microwave Wireless Sensors for Automotive Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This work initially presents an overview of the state-of-the-art and of the primary constraints of wireless sensors that are located on the charging stations (both hydrogen refueling and electric recharging stations), and on board of battery and fuel cell electric vehicles. Also, related legislative issues have been examined. Finally, a fully customized system designed for predictive maintenance and remote monitoring of working sections of automotive machineries is presented. A variety of wireless sensor nodes have been designed to be low-power, compact, energy-autonomous and located in close contact with key parts of a car engine compartment. The system is also composed of power sources able to transfer energy wirelessly directly to the sensor nodes in the form of electromagnetic waves, so they do not need the presence of batteries and their relative maintenance, also taking into account that they could be located in correspondence of awkward and metal-rich parts of the car engine compartment.

articleTitle: Dielectric Performance of Vegetable Oil-Based Nanofluid After Long-Time Aging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This study is focused on exploring how long-time aging affects the dielectric properties of an insulating nanofluid made of vegetable oil with the addition and SiC nanoparticles added at a particular concentration. AC and Lightning Impulse Breakdown Voltage tests, as well as partial discharge activity, are measured both for the aged nanofluid and matrix oil samples, and the outcomings are analyzed and contrasted with those after a one month-aging. The findings suggest that the integration of this filler type has led to stabilization of the dielectric behavior of the liquid, unlike the matrix which seems to be more influenced by the aging factors.

articleTitle: Electrical Flexibility Forecasting and Assessment for Heat-Pump-Based District Heating Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Nowadays, simple yet cost-effective solutions to extract flexibility from all possible energy devices are heavily investigated, together with optimal strategies to offer flexibility either in demand response programs or local flexibility markets (LFMs). In this context, this work proposes an Electrical Flexibility Forecasting Engine (EFFE) for district heating systems using centralised heat pumps. Starting from weather forecasts and electricity price signals, EFFE firstly forecasts the thermal power demand through an artificial neural network, and subsequently forecasts the electrical flexibility available over the desired time horizon. The idea is implemented in the case study of Culemborg (ND), demo site of the H2020-ACCEPT project, where EFFE is run in a typical winter day to forecast and asses both upwards and downwards flexibility, as well as the minimum economically viable bids to participate in a LFM.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning-Based Approach for Battery Life Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Battery technology advancement has been a significant obstacle in several energy fields. Research on battery management is crucial, both in theory and in practice, particularly for estimating battery states. Batteries exhibit robust, time-varying, and non-linear characteristics that are intricate. Hence, precisely determining their state and health status poses a difficult challenge. In this paper, we proposes a Long Short-Term Memory deep neural network for the classification of the battery life based on measurable data, specifically the current-voltage charge-discharge characteristics. Compared to other methods that are currently available in the literature, the proposed approach is able to achieve superior tracking performances, as evidenced by the experimental results obtained by using real measured data in the laboratory.

articleTitle: Assessment of Greenhouse Gas Emission Reduction Strategies in Electricity Grid of Turkiye by Utilizing EnergyPLAN Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This scientific paper investigates Turkiye“s ambitious plan to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by the year 2035. Employing EnergyPLAN, a simulation freeware designed for modeling national energy flows, a comprehensive analysis was conducted. Four distinct scenarios were meticulously crafted within the EnergyPLAN framework to assess the varying impacts of diverse technologies on greenhouse gas emissions. Given higher demand, a nuclear power plant, increased solar and wind capacities, the phased removal of coal power plants, waste-to-electricity conversion, and an additional nuclear power plant were considered. The study aims to provide valuable insights into the efficacy of different technological approaches, aiding policymakers in formulating effective strategies to achieve the targeted reduction in greenhouse gas emissions in the specified timeframe.

articleTitle: Real-Time Simulation of Island Electric System with Grid-Forming Controlled BESS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The paper presents the development of a dynamic simulation model of an island electric system for real-time simulation. The integration of a battery energy storage system (BESS) controlled in grid-forming mode is considered in the overall real-time model. The Simscape Electrical toolbox of MATLAB/Simulink is used for the development of the model, which is then deployed into an OPAL-RT device for the execution of simulations in real-time. The aspects related to the implementation of the island system for real-time simulation are discussed in detail. The possibility of an extended grid-forming control for the improvement of the dynamics of the system is also presented. Further developments of the work include the real-time examination of the island as a multi-energy system and real-time multi-site co-simulations for power hardware-in-the-loop experiments.

articleTitle: Investigating the Role of Electric Vehicles in Providing Frequency Response in Low-inertia Islanded Power Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The widespread integration of renewable energy resources (RERs) has brought significant changes to how future energy systems could be operated and planned. A key concern in these transformations is maintaining system frequency stability, particularly as the traditional inertia support from synchronous generation units becomes limited in future energy systems with converter connected RERs. This work explores the impact of flexible resources like electric vehicles (EVs) to offer flexibility for utilities during frequency disturbances in energy grids. One effective strategy involves simulating virtual inertia through controlling EV charging based on frequency derivatives. This study aims to explore how EVs can be leveraged as flexible resources to enhance the frequency response of energy systems. Therefore, it focuses on using the charging status of EVs as a control mechanism to provide flexibility, while employing a heuristic model to optimize virtual damping and inertia parameters of the control unit. Finally, this approach optimizes the response of EVs and investigates its impact on the energy system's frequency response.

articleTitle: The Potential of the 36 kV Voltage Level for Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The energy production from renewable energy sources and the accelerating trend of electrification are at the core of the energy transition. With a focus on the upcoming years, the transition aims to achieve low or zero carbon emissions, yet it expects a surge in electricity demand driven by the electrification of end-use consumption. Sustained by European regulations, this electrification is seen as the most effective means to accelerate the energy transition and decarbonisation, leading to enhanced efficiency, and reduced urban air pollution. However, these developments also pose challenges for the grid infrastructure and renewable energy deployment. The current layout of the distribution network faces the risk of collapse in the coming years due to the escalating electricity demand, particularly saturating the 20 kV main lines during peak load periods. Amidst these dynamics, the deployment of the new unified 36 kV voltage level also for the distribution network emerges as a promising solution for efficiently managing heavy loads while effectively managing costs and minimizing spatial requirements.

articleTitle: Graphene-Based Organic Polymer Composites for Improved Thermoelectric Properties Near Room Temperature
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Graphene/polymer composites are considered the most preferable materials in recent technology for energy harvesting applications. Herein, an efficacious and novel processing approach is applied to fabricate thin films using organic polymers i.e. Poly(3-hexylthiophene) (P3HT) with graphene-nanoplatelets (GNPs) composites. To improve the charge interactions and mobility throughout the composite, bis (trifluoromethane sulfonyl) imide (LiTFSI) and tert-butylpyridine (TBP) are adopted to dope P3HT. A research laboratory blade coater is used for the deposition of the GNPs:P3HT blend on glass slides. TE properties of the prepared films are measured on a homemade vacuum chamber setup. Seebeck coefficient, I-V, and P-V characteristics of the prepared films are comprehensively studied by varying the mass ratio of pristine/doped-P3HT composition with GNPs. We found that LiTFSI and TBP greatly increase the thermoelectric properties near room temperature.

articleTitle: Mathematical Model of Brushless Doubly Fed Induction Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: For powerful generators and powerful motors, brushless doubly fed induction machines (BDFIM) are used, representing a cascade of two induction machines. A mathematical model of the BDFIM without periodic coefficients is shown. The mathematical model is non-iterative, which requires a small computing resource for research, and which allows its inclusion in different types of power systems.

articleTitle: Techincal-Financial Assessentment of Offshore Wind Farm in Southern Brazil
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Offshore wind energy has become a prominent contender in the global landscape of renewable energy generation. The increase in its penetration can be attributed to various factors, including the implementation of supportive energy policies, heightened environmental awareness, and remarkable technological progress. In this context, the paper aims to evaluate the wind potential in the southern region of Brazil based on a technical-financial analysis of an offshore wind farm project. The applied methodology is supported by a survey of wind data for the region, including the selection of wind turbine models and the estimation of the project costs, such as the capital expenditure (CAPEX) and operational expenditure (OPEX). The study is focused on the evaluation of different energy transmission technologies. The assessment reinforces that the region has significant potential for energy production. The methodology can serve as a basis for implementing future projects.

articleTitle: K-Mean Algorithm to Support Energy Future Decision for Household with PV and EV
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This paper explores the application of the K-means clustering algorithm to analyze household energy data, focusing on electricity demand, photovoltaic (PV) generation, and electric vehicle (EV) charging. The objective is to identify distinct patterns of energy usage and generation, which can inform better energy management and decision-making strategies. Using data from a London household, we apply K-means clustering to segment the energy usage into meaningful clusters. The analysis reveals distinct profiles corresponding to different times of day and types of energy consumption and generation. Key findings suggest that clustering can effectively differentiate between high and low usage periods, the impact of PV generation on household energy dynamics, and the charging patterns of EVs. The results of this study provide valuable insights into how households can optimize energy consumption and leverage their PV and EV systems more effectively. Additionally, the paper discusses the implications of these findings for future energy policy and smart grid development. Recommendations are offered for integrating advanced data analytics into residential energy management systems to enhance sustainability and efficiency.

articleTitle: Toward Automation for Geographically Distributed Power Hardware-in-the-Loop Experiments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Geographically Distributed Power Hardware-in-the-loop (GD-PHIL) applications have been mainly intended as a way to interconnect several laboratories or research centers in order to share simulation hardware and computational resources; in such scenario, the co-simulating environment plays a crucial role in the process, as a sort of platform in which different resources from different manufacturers can communicate. In this paper, an automation strategy for GD-PHIL experiments is proposed. The details of the setup and automation procedure of GD-PHIL experiments are introduced. A case study with a Coordinated Voltage Control algorithm with two distance platforms/Research Infrastructures (RIs) is investigated to verify the feasibility of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Innovative Small Co-Generative CSP Plants Based on Molten Salts Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: ENEA in 2004 has started to test the mixture employment of Molten Salts (MS) fluid as Heat Transfer Fluid (HTF) in solar Parabolic Trough Collectors (PTC), at the experimental facility named PCS in the Casaccia Research Centre - Rome. The ENEA's experience of over twenty years qualification tests suggests that MS technology can be applied also to technology for small/medium Concentrating Solar Power (CSP) co-generative power plants. In the paper is proposed a system that uses a single tank molten salt storage integrated with a natural circulation Steam Generator (SG) side water. This system permits to easier the interface between a thermocline Thermal Energy Storage (TES) system and the end user that exploits steam for its thermal process. As part of this research, an experimental circuit was realized to test the concept. The experimental results have shown that the proposed technical solution can be used for the co-generation of heat and power also in small/medium scale. Moreover, the utilization of molten salts technology enables the coupling of multiple renewable energy sources. These findings are being leveraged for the modeling of a Digital Twin (DT) to further advance the understanding and optimization of such integrated energy systems.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of Multiconductor Cell Analysis by Overhead Line Field Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Multiconductor Cell Analysis (MCA) is a matrix algorithm computing the electrical steady-state regime of any asymmetrical multiconductor system. This paper presents an experimental validation of MCA, which is carried out by a measurement campaign performed on the Extra High Voltage (EHV) Dolo-Venezia Nord 18 km long double-circuit OverHead Line (OHL). By considering the double-circuit configuration of this line, it has been assessed the impact of one inducing circuit, kept in service, on the other circuit, kept out of service, for the evaluation of induced voltages and currents. One more time, comparisons between computations and measurements confirm the good agreement between MCA and the physical behavior of multiconductor systems.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Interferencies in Power Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This paper deals with the evaluation of electromagnetic interferences in the power networks 230 V 50 Нz with the help of special devices: Graham Stetzerizer meters, Greenwave Meters, PicoScope. Research was carried out at the different loads: led lamps and water pump, which worked in 10 modes. The impact of the use of filters on the power quality parameters of the electricity networks 230 V 50 Hz was investigated in range of frequency from 0 to 2 kHz. As a result, it was shown that the readings of the devices do not give an unambiguous representation of voltage quality, and the use of filters significantly increases the strength of the magnetic field emitted by the wires.

articleTitle: HVAC Submarine Cables Optimization Transmission Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Small groups of islands can be connected to the transmission grid through HVAC submarine cable line (CLs). Since the tourism sector has often a prominent role in their overall economy, the marked seasonal variation of the energy demand leads to an immediate impact on the cable loading. In low-load conditions, power losses along the cable are largely associated to its own charging currents. Power losses due to shunt reactors placed at both ends of the line are also considerable. Consequently, when low power flows are involved, the operation of the system at reduced voltages is required. The paper evaluates the opportunity of minimizing power losses as the transmitted active power changes by using Interconnection Transformers equipped with On-Load Tap Changers (OLTCs). The proposed solution aims to provide an accurate degree of control of the terminal voltages through the coordinated action of such devices.

articleTitle: A Jigsaw Approach for Electrical Engineering: Transient Stability Analysis of a Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This paper presents a structured pedagogical unit aimed at enhancing students' understanding of the transient stability of synchronous machines with excitation in response to a specific perturbation. The unit focuses on analyzing the effectiveness of two second-order models in studying stability, as well as examining the impact of inertia and dampers on transient stability. Utilizing Matlab software for simulation and analysis, the unit employs a methodology centred around group activities, role assignments, and collaborative problem-solving. Through theoretical introductions, practical activity, and result analysis, students engage in a comprehensive exploration of transient stability phenomena. The paper outlines the unit's objectives, methodology, activities, and evaluation criteria, providing insights into its implementation and potential benefits for student learning.

articleTitle: An AI-Based Algorithm for Energy Management of Hybrid Renewable Energy System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: In recent times energy demand has increased due to several factors, such as the growing world population, conventional ways of energy transmission & distribution, adopting less energy-efficient technologies, etc. These factors contribute towards more utilization of natural resources to meet the energy requirements, thus polluting the environment by producing harmful gases and increasing the energy cost. This paper addresses the aforementioned challenges, where it aims to look for more sustainable ways of energy production such as solar energy, wind energy, and biomass. This paper designed an off-grid system that aims to meet the University of Palermo's energy demand at a minimum annualized system cost. In this design, two ways are adopted for energy storage: 1) battery storage, and 2) hydrogen-based storage. The priority is to charge the batteries when excess energy is available. When the battery is fully charged and still some energy is available, this energy is used to operate the electrolyzer to produce hydrogen, which can also be used to produce again energy through fuel cells. This paper implemented an improved grey wolf optimization algorithm to find optimal power flow. The advantage of using it over other optimization algorithms is that it reduces premature convergence, and finds the global best solution. The result shows that, when the sources are not enough, the storage system can release enough energy for all time in the day.

articleTitle: PID Controller Design with a New Method Based on Fractionalized Integral Gain for Cruise Control System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: In this study, a fractionalized PID controller based on particle swarm optimization (PSO/FrPID) is presented for automobile cruise control systems. This system, known for its significant nonlinearity, has been linearized around its equilibrium point. In this method, the PID controller is designed using fractionalized integral and integer orders. This approach increases the parameters of the modified PID controller to four. The effectiveness of the proposed controller is evaluated in comparison to traditional PID methods, atomic search optimization (ASO/PID), particle swarm optimization (PSO/PID), and the genetic algorithm (GA-PID). The proposed methodology for the functioning of the vehicle cruise control system has proven to be superior to other promising methods documented in the literature, as confirmed by comparative evaluations that take into account both transient and frequency stability.

articleTitle: Influence of Microstructure and Design Features for an Anion-Exchange Membranes (AEM) Alkaline Water Electrolyzer Through Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The present study introduces a one- dimensional continuum electrochemical model for a single cell in anion-exchange membrane water electrolysis. This model incorporates the distributed porous electrode domain and the ion-exchange domain from the electrochemistry module of COMSOL Multiphysics. Validation against experimental polarization curve data shows significant agreement. The model allows studying the concentration and fluxes of electroactive species across cell thickness, providing insight into electrode utilization. The results show a significant impact of the AEM on the ion exchange mechanisms, with a special focus on the AEM thickness and the electrolyte water fraction. Additionally, the model capabilities as a useful design tool for optimization of the energy performance of the component.

articleTitle: Impact of Sequence Parameters in the Frequency Domain: Utilizing Physically Consistent Line Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of sequence parameters over a wide frequency range of an overhead transmission line when it considers the calculation of parameters of the line physically more consistent and soil properties that vary with frequency. For this purpose, it is calculated to the ground-return impedance and admittance of the transmission line using Petterson's approach, which employs a more rigorous voltage formulation. Additionally, in this calculation, soil properties were included using the frequency-dependent soil model. For comparison, the results from the ATP program, which employs in the calculation of parameters of the line Carson's approach, were used; this approach considers the less rigorous voltage formulation, assumes ideal ground conditions for ground-return impedance and admittance calculations, and does not consider frequency-dependent soil parameters. The results demonstrate that using physically more consistent line parameters and frequency-dependent soil parameters leads to significant differences in several parameters of homopolar and non-homopolar sequences. These significant differences are particularly notable in homopolar and non-homopolar resistances, homopolar inductance, homopolar capacitance, homopolar propagation velocity, and homopolar and non-homopolar attenuation constants.

articleTitle: Improving Low-Frequency Performance of Measurement Device for Frequency-Dependent Soil Properties
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: It has been shown previously that low-frequency resistivity should be measured at very low frequencies if accurate measurement of the imaginary part of the permittivity is necessary. In some cases, frequencies of 1 Hz or lower may be required. In accordance with these findings, a previously developed measuring device has been substantially modified to perform resistivity measurements at frequencies below 1 Hz and to improve the accuracy of low-frequency measurements in general. For this purpose, the clock generation frequency range for the analog-to-digital converter was increased. In addition, all coupling capacitors were removed and a bias voltage was used instead. To improve measurement accuracy (especially for the real part of the permittivity at low frequencies), the “first-in, first-out” memory size was increased. Some other improvements have also been made: the power supply and sine generator circuitry have been modified. A different analog-to-digital converter was used. The voltage measuring probe was also improved. Finally, the measuring device has been released as open source hardware. The circuit diagram, printed circuit board and source code are available at gitlab.com/dmika/epsilon.

articleTitle: Energy Community with Semi-Public System of EV Stations, Carport and Batteries Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The concept of energy community deals with electrical energy that is locally generated from renewable energy sources by installing photovoltaic panels or wind generators by some prosumers within the energy community. The energy excess compared with the consumption is injected in the upstream grid for economic benefits. The members of the community have flexibility in the energy use by installing storage systems and charging electric vehicles. The paper aims to present a way of working of an energy community in a residential complex of houses that invests in a semi-public system of charging stations, carport system with photovoltaic panels and storage of the energy produced. The environmental benefits and cost-benefit analysis of the project are presented.

articleTitle: Electrostatic Hazards in Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Static electricity poses significant hazards in industrial and daily settings due to the potential for igniting flammable atmospheres, causing electric shocks, and damaging electronic devices. This paper examines the generation and accumulation mechanisms of static charge, including contact/separation of solids and liquid flow. It discusses hazards associated with static discharge in explosive atmospheres and provides a practical criterion based on the minimum ignition energy for determining maximum acceptable resistance-to-ground values. Effective mitigation strategies are presented, such as grounding and bonding of conductive parts, use of static dissipative floors (resistance <100 MΩ), and footwear (resistance <100 MΩ or lower). A holistic approach combining these measures with proper area classification and personnel training is emphasized for safe operations in hazardous industrial environments involving flammable substances. Calculations and examples illustrate the principles and highlight the importance of controlling static electricity accumulation.

articleTitle: Gravure Printing for Sodium-ion Batteries Manufacturing: A First Attempt of Printed Cathode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The growing use of small, portable and wearable electronic devices enhanced the need of micro devices for their feeding, highly customizable to perfectly fit in. For such purpose the research is focused on printed batteries, thus printing technologies, as new sustainable processes for storage devices manufacturing. In particular, the here investigated gravure printing is able to couple high speed and high printing quality, and could be a low cost, low waste, high throughput, industrial candidate for the large scale production of batteries. To date, the industrial production in the field of printed batteries is limited to primary, not rechargeable devices, and most of the research refers to screen printing technique. In the last years, we demonstrated the feasibility of the most industrially appealing gravure printing for Lithium batteries (LiBs) manufacturing, successfully producing printed electrodes based on different active materials with performances, in terms of specific capacity, closed to the theoretical values. Moreover, the high homogeneity of the printed electrodes provides the stability of the performance over time and the long life cyclability. Here, following the most recent trend for going beyond the Lithium batteries, we propose an explorative work on the possibility to employ the gravure printing for Sodium-ion batteries (NaBs) manufacturing, showing a first attempt of printed cathode. Paying attention to the eco-sustainability of the involved materials and using a methodology based on the Capillary number, high printing quality was reached, guaranteeing the functionality; the performances required additional specific considerations.

articleTitle: Impact of Reservation on the Performance of Optimal Control in Electric Vehicles Fast Charging Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Service stations equipped with multiple delivery points for plug-in electric vehicles fast charging are expected to gradually replace petrol-based service stations. Operators interested in managing the new stations are going to face key challenges in terms of sizing the station's point of connection to the grid so as to render the provision of the service economically viable. As connection fees depend on the plant nominal power, sustainability is expected to come from the integration in the area of local generation from renewable energy sources and an electric energy storage device. This paper presents an approach based on optimal control methodology for regulating the energy flows at the point of connection of a service station with the grid. The control goal is to optimally balance the Plug-in Electric Vehicle (PEV) recharging power through the Energy Storage System (ESS), while also taking into account an uncertain number of charging requests and local generation. The overall objective is to lower as much as possible the power flowing at the point of connection with the grid, while providing as much as possible maximum power to the single PEVs. A model predictive control (MPC) algorithm is proposed to control the ESS. The single MPC iteration is based on continuous time optimal control. The core contribution of this paper is in the study of the impact of the level of uncertainty of the charging power (i.e., the number of charging requests by the PEV owners) on the performance of the controller. Simulation results show that reservations of the charging service represent a key aspect to take into account for taking decisions on the size of service station point of connection, even with the aforementioned control architecture.

articleTitle: Cyber Induced Harmonic Instability of Inverter-Based Renewable Generators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Extensive integration of inverter-based resources (IBRs) has introduced stability challenges to power grids due to their low-inertia nature and grid-following control configuration. To address these challenges, recent IEEE standards, e.g., IEEE 1547.1-2020, recommended grid-connected IBRs to provide grid-supporting functions, necessitating communication with utility control centers through various protocols. However, deployment of communication protocols exposes grid-connected IBRs to various threats originated from cyber-layer, endangering overall system stability. To make IBRs resilient to cyber-threats, knowledge about possible attacks and relevant consequences is required. On this basis, this paper emphasizes on vulnerability of grid-connected IBRs to a new family of resonance cyber-attacks. In this attack, the adversary induces harmonic instability by launching a resonance false data injection attack (FDIA) on the IBR's communication layer. To this aim, the attacker can take advantage of impedance-based models or frequency scanning approaches to determine the resonance frequency of the IBR with the grid. Through injecting sinusoidal noise within the resonance frequency range into the signals communicating between sensors or grid-supporting functions and IBRs, the adversary excites the resonance modes of the IBR with the grid, leading to instability of the inverter. The simulation results on a LCL-type grid-connected inverter demonstrated that this resonance FDIA can cause extensive current and voltage harmonic distortion at the inverter's point of common coupling (PCC), which can triggers protection devices and lead to inverter trip.

articleTitle: Low Temperature Carbon Electrodes for Low Light Performing Perovskite Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: In recent years, there has been growing interest among researchers in the development of photovoltaic (PV) cells specifically tailored for harvesting low-intensity diffused indoor light energy. A variety of PV materials have been utilized thus far in the quest to create efficient solar cells suitable for indoor applications. Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) can operate effectively under low-level injection conditions, such as low-light. Besides, carbon electrode gathered huge attention to substitute the instable and high-cost gold counter-electrode. Here, we present a PSC with carbon counter electrode formed by a lamination method with an efficiency close to 20% at indoor illumination. The hot-pressing method helps to enhance the conductivity of the carbon film and to improve the interfacial contact with the hole transporting layer. Moreover, the lamination protocol is compatible with the scaling-up of the PSC production.

articleTitle: A Novel Data-Driven Approach for the Simultaneous Prediction of State of Health Trajectory and Remaining Useful Life in Lithium-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: Due to the high implementation rate of Battery Energy Storage Systems in both the electric grid and the automotive industry, the development of a sophisticated Battery Management System (BMS) has become essential. The main task of a BMS is to ensure safety, while optimizing performance and useful life. BMSs rely, among other quantities, on accurate State of Health (SoH) assessment and Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction. This study presents a novel data-driven approach, based on recurrent neural networks, to simultaneously predict the RUL, defined as the number of remaining cycles before reaching 0.7 SoH, and to estimate SoH trajectory, which represents the sequence of predicted SoH for cycles above the threshold. The designed methodology leverages a padding system to handle inputs and outputs of varying lengths, allowing the same model to be used regardless of the number of cycles already performed on the cells. Two different padding systems were evaluated for output sequences: Last Observation Carried Forward (LOCF) 0.7 padding and padding with the arbitrary out-of-range value -1. The model trained with LOCF 0.7 padding showed better results, especially when tested on a narrower range than the one on which it was trained.

articleTitle: Visual Interaction and Its Effect on the Design of HV Towers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: The expected increase in renewable energy sources (RES) in the next decades is forcing Transmission System Operators (TSOs) to provide new electric infrastructures able to overcome possible congestions and allow a better integration of RES in the power transmission systems. Environmental interaction resulting from the physical presence of overhead lines (OHLs) represents one of the key aspects for the sustainability and public acceptability of new infrastructures. From an environmental perspective, the main interaction factors are the expected footprint, the visual effects and landscape aspects. As the towers represent the main visual interaction of an overhead line, new techniques and tools aimed to support the design of new infrastructures have been developed by Terna, the Italian TSO, for a better sustainable energy transition. The paper describes the mathematical model for a quantitative visual interaction evaluation of towers. Simulation results are reported comparing different standard and innovative tower topologies.

articleTitle: Analytical Data-Driven Method for Geomagnetic Disturbance Uncertainty Quantification Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Environment and Electrical Engineering and 2024 IEEE Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Europe (EEEIC / I&CPS Europe)
abstract: There is a fine tuning on the modeling of natural phenomena. One could have as goal to model in detail all events associated with a phenomena, however, this knowledge might not be readily available or can be difficult to obtain. Other goals could be model solution difficulty and impact on decision making. These are though competing and antagonistic goals, and one thus much find a compromise between model precision, solution and decision making. The question then is what to do when the modeling assumptions are not acceptable? The impact of models, considering reliability guidelines followed by the industry, towards planning for uncertainty when of extreme weather events, specifically geomagnetic disturbances, have been analyzed. While the previous work did quantify and qualify assumed modeling assumptions, it did not present any solution towards mitigating the effects of unacceptable estimation results. In this work authors present an analytical data-driven method for state estimation. The model provides acceptable modeling assumptions, i.e., results are statistically acceptable towards the ground-truth. In this work, towards phenomena modeling, experiment uncertainty is quantified through a data-driven approach. This quantification is then used, together with a measurement model, towards innovation estimation. Innovation is then used for prediction correction. Assumptions in this work are that one is able to quantify uncertainty source, through real-time measurements, and that ground-truth is provide by synthetic measurements through electromagnetic transient simulation. While the application domain chosen is geomagnetic disturbances, the presented method could be extended to other extreme weather events.
